title: Meals You Can’t Miss
editorial: Japan was remarkably consistent on food, but the queues weren't always worth obeying. Some of our best meals were simple breakfasts, standing sushi, or convenience-store finds.
Grilled-fish breakfast — Tokyo
Shinpachi Shokudo's grilled salmon breakfast was ¥680 when we visited. A proper breakfast for less than plenty of tourist snacks. We also liked its ginger-chicken set.
Ramen — Tokyo

Wakura's special ramen cost ¥1,350. Ramen Afro Beats' chicken-broth and spicy-miso bowls were ¥1,900 each: creamy, heavy, and with ridiculously good eggs. We couldn't finish all the noodles and broth.
Standing sushi — Tokyo
Uogashi Nihon-ichi's nine-piece Sakura selection was ¥2,000. Eating standing up is part of the experience. It also set a standard that cheaper conveyor-belt sushi didn't quite match.
Egg sando and onigiri — Tsukiji

Shouro's egg sandwich was incredible: cold, sweet milk bread, and a juicy egg filling. We also tried salmon, pork, and eel onigiri at the shop recorded in our notes as Onigiri Matuyoro, plus oysters at Saito's fish market. We skipped the longest queues.
Matcha — Tokyo and Miyajima

Funawa's soft serve in Asakusa had both creamy ice cream and a delicate cone. Tabanenoshi's matcha crème brûlée crêpe in Harajuku was ¥1,000. Itsuki Drops on Miyajima served matcha ice cream for ¥500.
Not every matcha dessert was a winner. The matcha momiji and Osaka's matcha melon bread were too sweet for us.
Wagyu — Kyoto and Osaka

Ginjiro in Pontocho was a highlight: lean wagyu at ¥1,200 and loin skewers at ¥1,400, both wonderfully tender. At Maido Wagyuyakiniku in Osaka, the cut recorded as “top stripe” was our favourite. Delicious, but rich; more fat isn't automatically more pleasure.
Budget sushi — Sushiro

Excellent for an enthusiastic sushi session without an equally enthusiastic bill. We recorded two pieces of salmon for ¥170 and eel for ¥230. It didn't taste as good as Uogashi, but the value was obvious.
Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki — Hiroshima

We tried Fumichan at Okonomimura: layers of cabbage, bean sprouts, pork, noodles, egg, and a crêpe, with cheese added. It's an experience worth describing, but not a personal favourite. The flavours didn't come together for us.
Convenience stores — everywhere
These aren't merely emergency food. A pork-and-egg rice bowl at 7-Eleven was ¥550; a grilled chicken thigh at Lawson was ¥150. They also rescued our Miyajima evening.
All prices above are observations from our September–October 2026 trip, not current menus.
